data.name: Brihadish
data.gender_notes: Brihadish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Brihadish is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Brihat', meaning 'extensive, large, or wide'. The suffix '-ish' denotes the one who possesses or rules over something. In Hindu mythology, Brihadish is considered the lord of the universe or the supreme deity, representing creation, preservation, and destruction. The name Brihadish carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Brihadish usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the infinite and eternal universe
data.etymology: Brihadish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Brihadish total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

In Hindu scriptures such as the "Atharva Veda" and "Mahabharata", Brihadish is considered the king of gods and the supreme ruler of the universe. The name holds a significant place in Hindu traditions and continues to be used as a name for deities and descendants.

historical_references.reference: Brihadishwas a renowned Hindu king of the Varmadeva dynasty in the 13th century CE. He ruled over the regions of present-day Maharashtra, India.

Another Brihadish, a prominent Jaina saint, lived during the 5th and 6th centuries CE. He was a disciple of Mahavira and is known for his teachings on ahimsa (non-violence) and the virtues of compassion and renunciation.
